def: A better instrument costs mass, power, data and money. You cannot improve one thing for free.
source: Space Mission Design Game challenge text

def: Spare capacity kept on purpose, because estimates grow and space is unpredictable. NASA concept designs keep about 25 to 30% on power and mass.
More power needs bigger arrays, which add mass, which needs more propellant, which adds more mass.
source: Derived from the rocket equation and power sizing

def: The change in speed a rocket gets depends on exhaust speed and the ratio of full to empty mass. Carrying fuel to move fuel makes mass expensive.
How efficiently an engine uses propellant, in seconds. Hydrazine thrusters are about 223 s.
Solar power drops with the square of the distance from the Sun. At Jupiter it is about 4% of what it is at Earth.
Spacecraft use special propellants such as hydrazine, which burn without air.
Instruments can make more data than the antenna can send. Data that never reaches Earth is not science.
Solar storms flip memory bits and add drag. Jupiter’s radiation belts damage electronics, so Europa Clipper hides them in a vault.
source: NASA Earthdata; JPL Europa Clipper pages

def: Once a design is approved it becomes a baseline. Changes go through a board and cost more the later they happen.
Risks are rated by likelihood and consequence, then accepted, mitigated or watched.
Specialists for each subsystem work together so a change in one area shows its effect on the others at once. This is why the game has four roles.
